evals.name: foundation-value-summary-with-appendix
evals.prompt: I'm putting together a five-slide value summary for the OpenSSF governing board. Slides: (1) members and what their memberships are worth today, (2) new memberships per year over the last five years, (3) developers who took part in OpenSSF projects over the last 12 months versus those who contributed code, (4) the top five contributing companies by code volume in that period, (5) governing board seats by company. Give me slide-ready figures with captions, and the data-notes appendix. Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Conventions fixed and stated (window as dates, org grain, population, scope per slide); OpenSSF resolved via search_projects and scoped as the foundation and its projects; memberships count and list-price value side by side; new memberships as a bare series by year with the current year marked partial and the grain named; participants vs contributors both stated; contributions by org ranking with the unattributed row dropped and its share stated once; board seats from the committee tools paginated and labelled visible to you; every figure cross-framed; a data-notes appendix in the Slide | Figure | Source | Coverage format with a label on every row and the run date in the header.
assertions: Conventions are stated (anywhere in the answer): the window as concrete dates, the organisation grain, the population policy (bots excluded, shares on the attributed base), and the scope of each slide (OpenSSF and its projects, resolved via search_projects)

Slide 1 presents the membership count and the list-price value side by side, never divided, with the count described as memberships (project-account pairs) and the value as list price rather than dues billed

Slide 2 uses the new-memberships family as a series by year without a hand-computed start date, quotes each year from its own row, marks the current year as partial, and names the grain (project memberships, not organisations)
Slide 3 states both figures: participants (any non-bot activity) for 'took part' and code contributors as the narrower reading, both distinct people, with the window as dates

Slide 4 ranks companies from the contributions family grouped by organisation with the unattributed row excluded from the ranking and the unattributed share stated once; the grain (account or parent) is said

Slide 5 takes board seats from the committee tools (the OpenSSF governing board found by project and name, roster paginated to the end, grouped by organisation client-side) and labels the figures as visible to the caller, never inferring seats from tier or activity
Every headline figure is cross-framed against a second reading (one scope level up, contributors ≤ participants, breakdown vs folded figure) and the check is recorded

The data-notes appendix has one row per figure in the Slide | Figure | Source | Coverage format, a label on every row from the closed list (governed / ad hoc / generated SQL / visible to you / interim / published / carried), the run date in the header, and every figure in the deck appears in the appendix and in the call log

The slide captions themselves (not only the appendix) carry the grain: memberships as project-account pairs rather than 'organisations', value as list price rather than dues; every share on a slide recomputes from the appendix rows

evals.name: company-briefing-microsoft
evals.prompt: Prepare the data for a Microsoft briefing deck: their Linux Foundation memberships and value (Microsoft alone and including subsidiaries), where they rank among members, their code contributions by project over the last 12 months (top ten projects), and who represents them on the CNCF and OpenSSF governing boards. Slide-ready figures plus the data notes, please. Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Legal name resolved (Microsoft Corporation) and the alone-vs-combined scope choice named on the first slide; memberships count and list-price value from two standard-metrics readings; rank read from a memberships-by-org ranking at a stated grain with 'among whom' said; contributions by project for the company with the window as dates and bots excluded; seats from committee tools per board, paginated, filtered on the organisation, labelled visible to you; peers or ranks never from hand-summed account rows; data-notes appendix with labels and the run date.
assertions: Microsoft is resolved to its stored legal account name before any figure, and the alone-vs-including-subsidiaries choice is named as a scope decision on the first slide with both readings given from separate standard-metrics calls
Membership count and list-price value are side by side and never divided; the reading is as of today
The rank is read from a memberships-by-organisation ranking ordered by value at a stated grain (account or parent), with 'among whom' said, and never from hand-summed account rows

Code contributions by project for the company use the contributions family with the company as the organisation, the window as concrete dates, bots excluded, top ten projects with the folded headline stated separately from the breakdown

Board representatives for CNCF and OpenSSF come from the committee tools (each governing board found by project and name, roster paginated to the end, filtered on the organisation), with name, role and voting status, labelled visible to the caller

The data-notes appendix has one row per figure with a label from the closed list, the run date, and every figure in the deck appears in the appendix and in the call log; the alone-vs-combined reconciliation (alone ≤ combined) is recorded

evals.name: coordination-section-reproducible-vs-cited
evals.prompt: Refresh the 'coordination engine' section of our membership deck: meetings hosted across the LF in the last 12 months, total hours of meetings, the top organisations by meeting attendance, and the chart of project communities hosted per year from the annual reports. Tell me which of these you can reproduce from LFX and how, and which must be cited from elsewhere, and give me the data-notes rows. Use the LFX MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Meeting aggregates read through the interim semantic-layer recipe as attendances (records) not people, labelled interim and floor; hours reported as an estimate or omitted with the reason (duration not on the attendance rows); top organisations by attendance on free-text organisation names with the vocabulary note and the unattributed share; the communities-hosted series cited to the annual reports as published, not rebuilt from the project index; the LF-wide scope with no project set; data-notes rows with the label per row.
assertions: The meeting count is given as distinct meeting occurrences (via the SQL assistant over the meeting-attendance data, labelled generated SQL, or via the interim recipe with attendances clearly distinguished from occurrences), labelled as a floor bounded by platform onboarding, never as an LF-wide total of people

Total hours are either summed scheduled duration over distinct occurrences from the SQL assistant (labelled generated SQL and floor), or an estimate explicitly flagged as an estimate with its method; never presented as measured people-hours or as attendances × an average
Top organisations by attendance are grouped on the free-text organisation name with the vocabulary note (not CRM legal names) and the unattributed share stated once

The project-communities-per-year chart is cited to the annual reports as a published figure (report and year) and is not rebuilt from the project index or the semantic layer; it is not reconciled against a warehouse figure
The LF-wide scope is stated with no project set (the umbrella foundation's slug is not used as the LF-wide scope)
Each item carries an explicit reproducible-vs-cited verdict, and the data-notes rows carry a label from the closed list per row and the run date

The SQL assistant was asked for distinct meeting occurrences and summed scheduled hours over the window, and the reported occurrence and hours figures are within a few percent of that reading (a row-capped or sampled estimate in place of it fails); no claim is made that a figure is unavailable from LFX when the SQL assistant can produce it
